He said "Pelasgian" because Euboea is near the Peloponnese, which was formerly called Pelasgia. The Macrones were neighbors of the Doliones. Some say the Macrieis are a tribe of the Becheires, who are always at war with the Cyzicenes. They had practiced the arts of war, as Philostephanus (fr. 4 M. III 29) and Herodorus (31 fr. 64 J.), who have written about their lives, record. Dionysius of Chalcis (fr. 10 M. IV 395) says they are called Macrones because they are colonists of the Euboeans. Others say they are called Macrones because there are more long-headed people among them, just as among the Persians there are hook-nosed people. Herodotus mentions them in Book 2 (104).
He called the war of the Macrieis "Pelasgian" because they are colonists of the Euboeans, and Euboea lies near the Peloponnese, which in ancient times was called Pelasgis.
